messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] treatment option
messages.body_plain:
The sign (- or +/ hypo or hyper) of the methylation difference will be
depending on which samples you designate as control and test. If you
just want differentially methylated regions/bases and do not care
about the sign of the methylation difference it doesn't matter which
samples are test and which samples are control, as long as some
samples are designated as control and some are designated as test you
will get differentially methylated regions.

Best,
Altuna

messages.subject: questions about read.bismark
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Two questions about this function:
1. does "nolap" parameter will throw away one entire end when the
paired-end overlap at least one base length?

The definition of nolap:
"   nolap: if set to TRUE and the SAM file has paired-end reads, the one
           read of the overlapping paired-end read pair will be ignored
           for methylation calling.
"
Bismark also has a scripts to extract the C site information, for this situation,
the overlaped region will be omitted when call methylation status, but other region that not overlapped will preserve.

2. Can "assembly" parameter be defined to non-model species?
The species I analyzed is not published yet. so this parameter will set to "foo", will this influence the results?

Thank you.

Best,
pch

messages.subject: Re: questions about read.bismark
messages.body_plain:
>
> 1. does "nolap" parameter will throw away one entire end when the
> paired-end overlap at least one base length?
>

It is supposed to throw away only the overlapping parts from one read. It shouldn't throw away the whole read unless the whole read is overlapping with the other read pair. This is designed to be similar to what bismark is doing.

> 2. Can "assembly" parameter be defined to non-model species?
> The species I analyzed is not published yet. so this parameter will set to "foo", will this influence the results?
>

assembly parameter can be any string, it will not effect the downstream analysis provided that you always operate on the same assembly. For example, do not try to merge objects from different assemblies, such as "hg18" and "hg19".

Best,
Altuna

> Thank you.

> Best,
> pch

messages.subject_clean: [methylkit_discussion] analyze data with more than 2 groups
messages.body_plain:
We haven't implemented that functionality yet but it is a theoretical and practical possibility. For more than 2 groups try to break your groups to meaningful pairs, if you can.

For additional covariates, it is also a possibility to add that to the regression (again not implemented) but that assumes every CpG will be affected by a covariate such as age, which is not the case. Only a small proportion of CpGs are affected by age. I guess that goes for other covariates. So I don't think it is a good idea to add covariates directly. Some preprocessing steps maybe necessary before adding covariates to the regression.

messages.body_plain:

messages.subject: Re: Methyl-kit error with calculateDiffMeth()?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ian,

I am posting this reply to you and methylKit Q &A forum (methylkit_...@googlegroups.com and reachable @ https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/methylkit_discussion).

You need to use unite() function before calling calculateDiffMeth() function. The unite() function finds bases/regions that are shared between all samples, and only then you can use the calculateDiffMeth() function. See the example code on the web page or the vignette.

For the second question, yes, you can look at custom regions. You need to have a GRanges object from GenomicRanges package that have the regions of interest. Then, you need to use regionCounts() function to summarize methylation information over regions. After that you need to use unite() and calculateDiffMeth()

Best,

Altuna
